result.title: SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting
result.summary: Real-world time series are frequently driven by exogenous events and structural shifts, rendering conventional forecasting based solely on historical numerical observations insufficient. While language models can retrieve external news, standard retrieval-augmented approaches struggle with high noise, missing signals, and an inability to reason causally about event impacts. We propose SEER (Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval), a closed-loop framework that dynamically optimizes event conditioning for time series forecasting. SEER translates prediction errors into two decoupled feedback mechanisms: (i) a reflective retrieval memory that refines subsequent search queries and filters spurious noise, and (ii) a persistent causal knowledge base that distills transferable domain dynamics. SEER enforces strict chronological boundaries across both event retrieval and reflection, preventing look-ahead bias and data leakage. Across six volatile time-series benchmarks, SEER consistently outperforms state-of-the-art time series foundation models and language model baselines.

AI.brief_summary: SEER 提出闭环框架，把时间序列预测误差转化为两类反馈：反思式检索记忆用于改写后续检索查询并过滤噪声，持久因果知识库用于沉淀可迁移的领域动态，并在检索与反思中严格保持时间顺序以避免前视偏差。
AI.relevance_reason: 时间序列预测与 LVR 主线较远，但其以预测误差驱动「检索—反思—过滤证据」的闭环，可能与 LVR 中何时获取新视觉证据、如何筛除无关证据并做停止决策的问题形成概念类比，可供核查。
